body:
Anya Patel: FYI customer on Enterprise SSO is hitting a login failure with GitHub OAuth. They see a UI error 'state verification failed' after redirect. Happening intermittently for ~30% users.
Leo Chen: got the screenshots? any pattern (prod vs staging, region)?
Anya Patel: sent screenshots in DM and pasted the error message. All prod users, behind our EU edge gateway. They say it works if they manually remove the trailing segment from the callback URL.
Jess Rivera: that smells like our proxy normalizing or stripping a path segment on 301/302. Which callback do we register for that org?
Anya Patel: registered redirect in GitHub app is https://app.redwood.example/auth/oauth/callback/sso (with the /sso). The browser callback that reaches our app shows /auth/oauth/callback instead (no /sso).
Samir Gupta: can you grab the gateway logs around the time of a failed login? specifically the incoming redirect request from github (GET /auth/oauth/callback/sso?code=...&state=...) and what we forwarded upstream. If the gateway rewrote path that'll explain state mismatch because GitHub expects exact redirect_uri match.
Console Bot: log snippet attached (redacted):
```
[2026-03-12T13:22:04Z] edge-gw-12 GET /auth/oauth/callback -> 302 -> upstream /auth/oauth/callback/sso?code=***&state=abc123
[2026-03-12T13:22:04Z] edge-gw-12 forwarded GET /auth/oauth/callback/sso?code=***&state=abc123
[2026-03-12T13:22:04Z] app-01 received GET /auth/oauth/callback?code=***&state=abc123
```
Anya Patel: note how forwarded vs received differ — looks like the gateway stripped the /sso in the final request path to the app. That would cause our session/state lookup to miss the saved nonce tied to /sso namespace.
Leo Chen: root cause: some edge configs canonicalize paths by trimming 'trailing path segment when proxy target has a base path' — I remember a recent change to the rewrite rules. Samir, can you check the recent deploy that touched edge rewrite behavior?
Samir Gupta: checking — rolled deploy 2234498000 had a change to 'strip_base_path' to handle old vanity routes. Reverting for one org might fix but risky. Short-term workaround: ask customer to update their GitHub OAuth app redirect to the canonical path without /sso (https://app.redwood.example/auth/oauth/callback) — should match what our app actually receives. Also advise them to clear cookies to avoid stale state.
Jess Rivera: we should give the customer clear repro + steps and a temporary safe workaround. Also flag as P1 for Dedicated/Enterprise since user login impacted.
Anya Patel: message to customer drafted: "We're seeing the edge gateway rewrite the callback path which causes GitHub's redirect_uri not to match the registered app value, resulting in state verification failures. As a temporary workaround either update the OAuth app's redirect URI to remove the trailing segment or we can roll back the edge rewrite for your tenant. Please confirm if you want us to change the redirect on our side or if you can update the GitHub app settings."
Leo Chen: internal next steps: (1) eng-infra to evaluate quick rollback for tenant 89-org (Samir) (2) product to notify other orgs that might use path-based callbacks (Jess) (3) add integration test simulating redirect URI rewrite.
Samir Gupta: created infra ticket INF-2026-119, linked to this thread. I'll attach the config diff and plan a canary revert for tenant 89.
Jess Rivera: tagging @eng-infra and @product. Anya, pls send the workaround to the customer and request a repro timestamp and user agent for next hit so we can tie to logs. :thumbsup:
